title: Numbers, time and days
can: Count to 100, tell the time, arrange when to meet and understand prices.
doneText: You can now count, tell the time, arrange to meet on a day and at a time, and follow prices.

discover.intro: All of these sentences tell the time. Spot why the blue ones say heure and the orange ones say heures.

groups.label: Blue
lines: Il est une heure et demie.

groups.label: Orange
lines: Il est cinq heures et quart.
Il est dix heures moins le quart.

discover.question: Why heure in blue and heures in orange?
options: One o'clock is one hour, so it is singular: une heure. From two on it is plural: deux heures.
Blue sentences are in the morning and orange ones are in the afternoon.
Heure is formal and heures is informal.
discover.nudge: Not quite. Look at the number just before heure or heures in each colour.
discover.reveal: Une heure is one hour, so it is singular. Two o'clock and later are plural: deux heures. Add the minutes straight after, or use et quart, et demie and moins:

hooks.title: The clock: et and moins
rows: Il est quatre heures et quart.
Il est une heure et demie.
Il est six heures moins vingt.
Il est neuf heures moins le quart.

learn.title: The numbers
learn.sub: Tap any number to hear it

blocks.text: From 21 to 69, add the units after the tens: vingt-deux, trente-cinq. With one, use et and no hyphen: vingt et un, trente et un. From 70, French counts on from twenty: soixante-dix is sixty-ten, and quatre-vingts is four twenties.
Belgium and Switzerland say septante and nonante, which are easier. In France, people will not use them, so learn soixante-dix and quatre-vingt-dix.

blocks.title: Lundi or le lundi
a: On Monday (this coming one), I'm working.
blocks.note: French has no word for on with days. With no word, you mean this coming day. With le, you mean every week. Days start with a small letter.

blocks.text: This is the opposite of Spanish. In Spanish, el lunes is this Monday and los lunes is every Monday. In French, lundi is this Monday and le lundi is every Monday.
In writing and on timetables, France uses the 24-hour clock: 20 h 30. In speech, people say huit heures et demie du soir. Many shops close on Sundays, and small shops may close for lunch.

phrases.es: Il est deux heures et demie.

exercises.why: One o'clock is one hour: une heure.

exercises.q: Il est quatre heures et quart.

exercises.say: Il est dix heures moins le quart.
exercises.why: Moins le quart means quarter to: ten minus a quarter is 9:45.

items.full: Il est une heure et demie.
Il est douze heures moins cinq.
Il est huit heures du soir.
Il est onze heures et quart.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.
exercises.why: At a time is à: à huit heures.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.
exercises.sentence: Il est trois heure et quart.
exercises.fixed: Il est trois heures et quart.
exercises.why: From two on, heures has an s: trois heures.

answer: il est deux heures et demie
exercises.why: Two is plural, so deux heures. Half past is et demie.
Le lundi means every Monday. Without le, lundi means this coming Monday.
5:40 is twenty to six: six heures moins vingt.

exercises.prompt: Let's meet on Saturday at nine.
exercises.why: Samedi for one day, with no word for on, then à for the time.
C'est combien ? is the everyday way. Ça fait combien ? is for the total.
From 21 up: tens, then units. Quarante-cinq.

exercises.prompt: A friend says rendez-vous à vingt heures. When is that?
exercises.why: Vingt heures is 20:00 on the 24-hour clock, so 8pm.
Every Monday takes le: le lundi.

write.title: Say it in your own words
write.task: Make a plan with a friend: suggest a day and a time to meet, and say how much something costs.
write.model: Rendez-vous samedi à huit heures et demie. Ça coûte quinze euros.
checklist: The day has no word for on
The time uses à and heures
Numbers from 21 up join with a hyphen: vingt-cinq

boss.title: Train tickets at Gare de Lyon
boss.persona: You are Madame Girard, a ticket clerk at Gare de Lyon in Paris. The learner is buying a train ticket. Talk about days, departure times and prices, using numbers and times often. Address the learner as vous. Keep every message to one short sentence.

turns.npc: Bonjour. Vous voulez un billet pour quel jour ?
turns.en: Hello. Which day do you want a ticket for?
choices: Pour samedi, s'il vous plaît.
Pour le samedi, s'il vous plaît.
Le samedi means every Saturday. For one trip, say samedi.
Pour en samedi, s'il vous plaît.
There is no word for on with days: pour samedi.

turns.npc: Il y a un train à dix heures et quart et un autre à midi et demi.
turns.en: There is a train at quarter past ten and another at half past twelve.
choices: À dix heures et quart, s'il vous plaît.
En dix heures et quart, s'il vous plaît.
At a time is à: à dix heures et quart.
À dix heure et quart, s'il vous plaît.
From two on, heures has an s: dix heures.

turns.npc: Très bien. Ça fait douze euros cinquante.
turns.en: Very good. That's twelve euros fifty.
choices: Douze euros cinquante ? Voilà.
Vingt euros cinquante ? Voilà.
Vingt is 20. Douze is 12.
Deux euros cinquante ? Voilà.
Deux is 2. Douze is 12.

turns.npc: Merci. Le train arrive à onze heures moins dix.
turns.en: Thank you. The train arrives at ten to eleven.
choices: À dix heures cinquante ? Parfait, merci.
À onze heures dix ? Parfait, merci.
Moins dix means ten to eleven, so 10:50, not 11:10.
À neuf heures dix ? Parfait, merci.
Onze is eleven. Onze heures moins dix is 10:50.

boss.closingEn: You're welcome. Have a good trip.
boss.chatOpening: Vous voulez aussi un billet retour ?
boss.chatOpeningEn: Do you also want a return ticket?
